recommendation_reason: The dominant, robust, cross-seed-identical driver of the known-family calibration failure is loop-grid (and, more mildly, branched-loop) -- families with more than 4 junctions -- while golden-reference (exactly 4 junctions) passes robustly on every seed. The exchangeability audit traced this to a concrete, deterministic mechanism: `run_m7_topology._generate_eval_scenarios`'s `EVAL_MAX_SOURCES=4` (combined with alphabetically-sorted-then-truncated junction selection) means development-holdout scenarios for loop-grid only ever exercise 4 of its 8 junctions (J1-J4; J5-J8 never appear) and branched-loop only 4 of its 7 (JA-JD), while the calibration pool draws source nodes from the FULL junction set via a different, less-truncated construction. This is a genuine calibration-vs-development population mismatch, not a conformal-code defect (the implementation audit and the exact Section-5 reproduction gate both clear the conformal machinery itself) and not primarily a support, overconfidence, or score-choice problem (H1/H3/H8 not the primary drivers).
strongest_evidence: Family-pooled (n=112/seed) development coverage under the frozen CURRENT_FAMILY_DEPTH scheme: golden-reference 0.946-0.955 (Wilson 90% CI entirely above 0.85 on all 3 seeds), loop-grid 0.712-0.732 (CI entirely below 0.85 on all 3 seeds, upper bound never exceeding 0.795). Within loop-grid, source node J1 has coverage exactly 6/28=0.214 on all 3 seeds (development scenarios are a shared, non-resampled pool by M9.0a's own design) while J2-J4 range 0.82-1.0. The development-oracle counterfactual requires a robust +0.04 to +0.057 quantile shift (all 3 seeds) to reach the coverage the CURRENT_FAMILY_DEPTH scheme's calibration-derived quantile does not provide -- and every alternative M9.0b grouping scheme (family:depth, pooled-depth, broad-fallback) yields the SAME loop-grid MATURE coverage (0.75), proving the failure is not a grouping-choice problem.
evidence_against: The J1-specific difficulty within loop-grid (consistently confused with J7/J8 at every prefix depth) is not fully explained by the truncation mechanism alone -- truncation explains WHICH nodes are tested in development, not why J1 is intrinsically harder than J2-J4 (which ARE in the tested subset and pass comfortably). A genuine structural/hydraulic source-discrimination difficulty specific to J1 may coexist with the dataset-construction issue.
cross_seed_consistency: ROBUST for every finding cited in strongest_evidence -- identical family ordering (golden-reference > branched-loop > loop-grid), identical source-node pattern within loop-grid (J1 exactly 0.214 on all 3 seeds), and same-sign, comparable-magnitude required_quantile_shift on all 3 seeds.
limitations: The calibration pool's own source-node distribution was not directly instrumented in this milestone (only inferred to be less-truncated than development's, from code reading of `_family_scenario_pool` vs `_generate_eval_scenarios`) -- direct verification would strengthen H7/H2 further but was not attempted to avoid any risk of modifying frozen M7/M9.0 code.
Per-depth development coverage estimates (n=16) carry wide descriptive uncertainty (Section 8); the primary claims in this closure rely on family-pooled (n=112) estimates, which are much tighter.

H3 (overconfidence) could only be tested on golden-reference, the one family ARM_A and ARM_B2 share -- it cannot be directly ruled out for branched-loop/loop-grid specifically, though no other evidence in this study points toward overconfidence as those families' driver.
Full repository test suite was not run to completion in this environment (runtime); focused M9.3 tests, relevant M9.0a/M9.0b/M9.1/M9.2 regression tests, and pyright were run instead.
This closure does not evaluate or authorize any specific fix to `run_m7_topology.py`'s evaluation-scenario generator -- that remains for a future, separately-scoped milestone.
